bib.title: MIRAGE: Scaling Test-Time Inference with Parallel Graph-Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning Chains

legacy_report:
SOURCE: MIRAGE: Scaling Test-Time Inference with Parallel Graph-Retrieval-Augmented Reasoning Chains. Kaiwen Wei, Rui Shan, Dongsheng Zou, Jianzhong Yang, Bi Zhao, Junnan Zhu, Jiang Zhong (Chongqing University; CAS Institute of Automation). arXiv:2508.18260v2 (18 Jan 2026). The copyright line reads "Copyright © 2026, Association for the Advancement of Artificial Intelligence", so it looks like an AAAI 2026 camera-ready. The text never says "accepted at". Treat it as arXiv v2 in AAAI format. Code: github.com/Despacitobei/MIRAGE.

COVERAGE: I read 0 to 42,500 and 44,500 to 49,717 of 49,717 chars. I skipped 42,500 to 44,500, which is mid-reference-list. The extraction ends at the references. The text cites Appendices A to E (prompts, Algorithm 1, dataset statistics, implementation details, human-eval metric), but none are in this PDF's text. I could not read them, so hyperparameters and prompts are unavailable.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- Claim: MIRAGE has the best average GPT-4o rank on all three benchmarks, and the best ExplainCPE accuracy among the methods compared, using QwQ-32B as the backbone.
  number: GenMedGPT-5k rank 1.8 (next best Search-o1 3.3). CMCQA rank 2.8 (Search-o1 3.0). ExplainCPE rank 3.1, tied with MindMap, and accuracy 84.8% (MindMap 84.6%, BM25 83.5%, QwQ-32B alone 82.8%, GPT-4o 77.8%).
  setup: QwQ-32B backbone for decomposer, retriever and synthesizer. 32,768-token max input. Datasets GenMedGPT-5k (EMCKG), CMCQA and ExplainCPE (CMCKG), following the MindMap protocol. Rank is the average GPT-4o listwise rank, lower is better.
  quote: "on GenMedGPT-5k, it reaches a rank of 1.8, and on ExplainCPE, it achieves 84.8% accuracy"
  where: Main Results, p.5 (about char 15,500)
  Reading the table, the margins are small except on GenMedGPT-5k. MIRAGE is not the best on every BERTScore column, and its ExplainCPE F1 (0.888) is below MindMap's (0.889). The text's "consistently achieves the best" is stronger than the table.
- Claim: The result holds with a different backbone.
  number: ExplainCPE with DeepSeek-R1-32B: MIRAGE rank 2.9, accuracy 84.4%. MindMap (DS) 84.1%, Search-o1 (DS) 81.1%, DeepSeek-R1-32B alone 82.2%.
  setup: ExplainCPE only, and all baselines moved to the same backbone.
  quote: "MIRAGE (DS) 0.8870.883 0.885 2.9 84.4%"
  where: Table 2
- Claim: Human judges agree with the GPT-4o ranking, and MIRAGE wins most pairwise comparisons.
  number: MIRAGE wins 77% vs GPT-4o, 69% vs GPT-4o+ToT, 60% vs QwQ-32B, 48% vs BM25, 51% vs Embedding Retriever, 45% vs MindMap, and 40% vs Search-o1. Losses against Search-o1 and MindMap are about 31%.
  setup: 100 random GenMedGPT-5k examples. Two medical graduate students. Pairwise comparison of factual accuracy, reasoning clarity and clinical fluency.
  quote: "we conduct a human study on 100 randomly sampled examples from GenMedGPT-5k. We recruit 2 medical graduate students"
  where: p.5 and Figure 4. I mapped the Figure 4 percentages to baselines by the figure's order. The extraction is jumbled, so treat the per-baseline mapping as approximate.
- Claim: The decomposer and synthesizer both help (ablation).
  number: Average win/tie/lose of full MIRAGE against each ablation: w/o Decomposer 40.72/44.97/14.31, w/o Synthesizer 44.03/43.23/12.73, w/o both 48.27/38.68/13.05.
  setup: GPT-4o pairwise judge, order swapped and averaged. The metrics are illness identification, treatment suggestion and overall correctness. The paper does not state which dataset the ablation used.
  quote: "Average 40.72 44.97 14.31 44.03 43.23 12.73 48.27 38.68 13.05"
  where: Table 3
- Claim: Over-decomposition hurts, while more retrieval budget has diminishing but positive returns. The retriever is demand-driven and stops early.
  number: Defaults are Nq=4 sub-questions and Nr=5 retrieval steps. Both were swept from 5 to 10 in the figure. The text gives no numbers for the curves.
  setup: Average GPT-4o rank across datasets plus ExplainCPE accuracy. On dialogue-style CMCQA, going from Nq=1 to 2 can lower performance.
  quote: "performance may even drop from Nq = 1 to Nq = 2, likely due to disrupted contextual flow"
  where: Further Analysis, Figure 3
- Claim: Baseline findings. Reasoning models beat prompt-only ToT, and static text retrieval is unstable. KG retrieval (MindMap) is more consistent. Search-o1's web retrieval degrades on ExplainCPE.
  number: QwQ-32B 82.8% vs GPT-4o+ToT 80.2% on ExplainCPE. Search-o1 80.7%.
  quote: "Search-o1 performs competitively on GenMedGPT-5k and CMCQA but drops notably on ExplainCPE, likely due to noisy web content."
  where: Main Results
- Claim (method): The pipeline has four parts. A question decomposer makes entity-grounded sub-questions, only when a query has several distinct medical entities, and at most Nq of them. Parallel chains retrieve from the KG in two modes. Anchor mode takes the neighbourhood of one matched entity, with at most k neighbours per relation. Bridge mode takes typed paths of length up to h between two entities. A synthesizer checks the answers against each other. A coordinator holds shared state.
  number: none
  setup: Entity matching by embedding similarity above a threshold τ. If nothing matches, a "no entity match" token is returned so the model reformulates. Triples are verbalized as "e0 r e1" between <|KG_RESULT_BEGIN|> and <|KG_RESULT_END|>. Relation types are limited to a curated clinically validated set.
  quote: "Bridge Mode is triggered when two entities are identified, retrieving direct or multi-hop paths connecting them."
  where: Method, pp.3-4
- Claim (method): Cross-chain verification is a heuristic. On conflict, the synthesizer keeps the answer whose chain set covers a broader neighbourhood of corroborating relations or fits the query better. It flags KG-level contradictions such as a drug that both treats and causes a symptom. It then writes the final answer and an audit record of decomposition, retrieval and synthesis.
  number: none
  quote: "This majority-based verification strategy prefers answers supported by multiple independently retrieved evidence chains"
  where: Answer Synthesis section

LIMITS
- There is no Limitations section. The conclusion makes no concessions.
- Evaluation depends heavily on GPT-4o as judge. Only one 100-example, 2-annotator human check on one dataset (GenMedGPT-5k) supports it. No inter-annotator agreement and no confidence intervals are reported.
- The ablation shows no per-dataset breakdown, and many outcomes are ties.
- No cost or latency data is given, although "test-time scaling" and "efficient utilization of computational resources" are claimed. There is no token count or wall-clock comparison with Search-o1 or the single chain. Parallel chains are never compared against equal-compute baselines such as self-consistency or ToT on the same backbone. The only ToT baseline is GPT-4o+ToT.
- Only medical QA is covered, with pre-built curated KGs from MindMap. The paper does not show KG construction, Cypher or text-to-query generation. Retrieval is embedding entity linking plus fixed neighbour and path expansion.
- The synthesizer "allows fallback to medical priors when the knowledge graph is silent", so the answers are not purely KG-grounded.
- The traceability and interpretability claims are not measured quantitatively. They rest on the case study (Figure 5).
- The gap over MindMap and Search-o1 is small on CMCQA and ExplainCPE. The DeepSeek backbone test covers ExplainCPE only.

BUILDS ON
- MindMap (Wen, Wang, Sun, ACL 2024): datasets, KGs, evaluation protocol and baseline.
- Search-o1 (Li et al. 2025a): agentic search inside reasoning, the main baseline.
- ARise (Zhang et al., ACL 2025).
- Tree of Thoughts (Yao et al., NeurIPS 2023).
- Graph of Thoughts (Besta et al., AAAI 2024).
- Chain-of-Thought (Wei et al., NeurIPS 2022).
- Self-Consistency (Wang et al., ICLR 2023).
- ReAct (Yao et al., ICLR 2023).
- Self-RAG (Asai et al., ICLR 2024).
- RAG (Lewis et al., 2020).
- GraphRAG (Edge et al. 2024, arXiv).
- Test-time scaling (Snell et al. 2024, arXiv).
- DeepSeek-R1 (2025, arXiv).
- QwQ-32B.
- BERTScore (Zhang et al., ICLR 2020).

CODE: none in the text. The retrieval-block markers are quoted above. The prompts and Algorithm 1 are in Appendices A and B, which are not in the extraction.

FIGURES (one candidate): Figure 2, "Overview of the proposed MIRAGE framework", p.3. It shows the decomposer fanning out to n parallel chains. Each chain runs think, KG_QUERY, Anchor or Bridge retrieval, and KG_RESULT. The chains are then verified and synthesized. It explains the architecture and the two retrieval modes faster than prose. Figure 1 compares Static RAG, Agentic RAG, ToT and MIRAGE.

NOTE FIT: Note 11 (kg-rag-and-text-to-cypher) fits only partly. MIRAGE is KG-RAG with agentic, tag-triggered retrieval (single-entity neighbourhood and entity-pair paths) and has no text-to-Cypher. It suits the KG-RAG half of note 11 as a retrieval-pattern example. Notes 05-topology-patterns (fan-out and verifier/synthesizer) and 07-failure-modes-at-scale (error accumulation in linear chains) are alternative homes for the parallel-chains-plus-cross-verification claim. Note 12 (KG as shared agent memory) is a weak fit. I did not read the notes, so this is judged from titles only.

PROBLEMS: The extraction is clean text, but the figure text is jumbled (Figure 4 percentages and Figure 3 axes). The appendices A to E are referenced but not present, so I could not read them. No embedded instructions were found.
